title: Beazley Security Q3 report: exploited vulnerabilities start 28% of ransomware cases
geo_basis: global report; pin is a placeholder for the United States
summary: Insurance Business reports that Beazley Security's Q3 threat report says ransomware cases starting with an exploited vulnerability rose from 14% in Q2 to 28% in Q3. It cites about 37,000 publicly disclosed vulnerabilities in Q3, up nearly 80% on Q2, and four ways attackers bypassed MFA. Beazley's CEO advises starting with known exploited vulnerabilities and internet-facing applications.
plain: Beazley Security says more ransomware attacks now begin with an exploited software flaw: 28% in Q3, up from 14% in Q2, as reported by Insurance Business.
exec: Beazley's data, as reported, shows exploited vulnerabilities starting 28% of ransomware cases, up from 14% in Q2.
action: Start with known exploited vulnerabilities and internet-facing applications, as Beazley's CEO advises, and check whether your MFA is phishing-resistant.

sources.name: Insurance Business: Cyberattack tactics are outpacing what renewal forms ask

date_note: Dated by the trade article's publication day; the Beazley report itself was not read.

validation.note: Only Insurance Business read; Beazley's own report not read.
